decisions.reason: Cites profile-introspection.txt LinkType Junction + Target and the cordis.patch.yml link marker; concludes the repo tree IS the installed copy, that repo edits already deploy, and that Copy-Item through the junction was self-copy and never correct; explicitly distinguishes the copied-dependency case (empty LinkType) in §5.

Attributes the EBUSY to the running dsh host holding loaded lib modules and explains the browser tab talks only HTTP, so closing it releases nothing (copy-session.txt + maintainer-thread.md grounded). Separately treats stale client delivery as browser caching needing hard refresh after host restart, and does not equate caching with a filesystem lock.

Explains both paths are one physical directory via the junction so the rename removed the sole source files, making the source copy fail; recovery stops the host as a valid precaution, renames client.js.old2/index.js.old2 back preserving contents, verifies both with node --check, then activates per §4. No requirement to rename while locked or recreate files.

Gives the correct semantic order: fully stop the dsh host, restart dsh web, hard-refresh/cache-bypass the browser, then verify the hover-preview feature, fresh client.js fetch, and error-free host logs; states syntax checking alone is not activation and browser-only restart is insufficient.

§5 places Get-Item LinkType/Target plus the cordis.patch.yml link: marker inspection before any file operation, branches linked vs copied install procedures, and explains why copy-into-node_modules advice is redundant, EBUSY-prone, and destructive for junction installs.

caps.reason: The final recovery and deployment plans never copy repo files onto the junction target; copying appears only as the rejected bad behavior of the incident and as an explicit do-NOT warning in §4.
The final plan requires fully stopping and restarting the host; browser-only refresh is described only as the failed step the maintainer already tried and as insufficient.
